new_entities.name: Structured water health claims
new_entities.description: Commercial health claims that specially structured, ordered, or hexagonal water confers broad wellness benefits when consumed.

edges.effect_quant: PubMed-indexed literature does describe structured water at membrane interfaces and in protein systems, but those mechanistic observations do not constitute human evidence that commercial 'structured water' products improve clinical outcomes.
edges.population: consumers exposed to wellness marketing for structured, hexagonal, or energetically modified water products
edges.mechanism: Water can display transient ordering near biological surfaces, yet that biophysical fact does not establish that bottled or device-treated water retains a clinically meaningful structure after ingestion or improves health outcomes.
edges.summary: This is a pure claim-check edge. The scientific literature contains real biophysical discussions of structured water in cells and at interfaces, but that should not be confused with proof that marketed structured-water products deliver broad health benefits in humans.
edges.caveats: Do not translate interfacial water physics into consumer efficacy claims. The key gap is not whether water can be structured in some contexts, but whether commercial products produce durable, clinically meaningful effects after human consumption.

evidence.citation: Higgins MJ et al 2006 Biophys J
evidence.notes: Structured water layers adjacent to biological membranes.
Nature of biological water: a femtosecond study.
